subject: Re: SIG follow-up — SCIM mapping sample & least-privilege clarification
messages:
From: Jennifer Peters <jennifer.peters@acme.com>

Subject: SIG follow-up — SCIM & RBAC evidence needed

Marcus —

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Acme's security team has one follow-up for the SIG: can you provide a sample SCIM attribute mapping (with the minimum attributes you expect) and a short explanation of how Redwood enforces least-privilege for roles created via SCIM? We also have a few questions about RBAC scopes for service accounts.

Deliverables we'd like:
- SCIM attribute mapping (CSV or JSON) showing required vs optional attributes
- Short note on how autogenerated roles are scoped and how MFA/service-account restrictions apply
- Any sample logs or evidence that show provisioning events (we can accept event IDs or a sanitized sample)

Can you get these to us by next week? Happy to jump on a quick call if needed.

Best,
Jennifer
Security Program Manager
Acme Corp

Thanks Jennifer — we can absolutely provide that. Quick plan:

1) I'll attach a minimal SCIM mapping CSV that highlights required attributes we push (externalId, userName, name.givenName, name.familyName, emails[type=work], active).
2) Dev will capture a sanitized provisioning log snippet (timestamp + event id + user id) showing a create/update/delete flow.
3) Laura and Marissa will draft a short note on RBAC scoping and how we apply least-privilege and MFA exceptions (service accounts vs user accounts).

One clarification: when you say "service accounts" — do you mean API keys/long-lived tokens for integrations, or machine identities created via SCIM? The controls differ and we want to provide the right evidence.

I'll get the mapping + log snippet attached and loop back with the RBAC note.

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jennifer Peters <jennifer.peters@acme.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — SCIM & RBAC evidence needed

Jennifer/Tom —

Attached is a sanitized provisioning log extract (CSV) and a small diagram showing our token/credential lifecycle. Notes:
- Machine identities created via SCIM are created in a sandboxed tenant role: they are not assigned any admin-level policies by default.
- Role assignment is a separate step: our SCIM service writes the user/group membership and then a policy engine (RBAC service) evaluates attribute-based rules before any privileged role is granted.
- MFA: machine identities do not perform interactive MFA. For human users we require MFA on first-time SSO login and for high-risk actions; for machine identities we require short-lived tokens (default 1h) and recommend signed JWTs with rotation.

See attachments: scim_attribute_mapping.csv, token-lifecycle-diagram.png

Happy to provide a short (1-page) RBAC scope matrix next.

—Dev
Senior Platform Engineer, Identity
Redwood Inference

(attachments: token-lifecycle-diagram.png)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — SCIM & RBAC evidence needed

Jennifer —

Attached is the RBAC scope matrix PDF that maps common scopes (read:logs, write:models, admin:billing) to the default role groups and notes whether those can be assigned via SCIM. Key points:
- SCIM only writes membership to groups. Groups in Redwood are mapped to least-privilege role templates by default.
- Admin-level roles cannot be assigned by SCIM users unless additionally approved by a human reviewer (audit trail and approval ticket required).
- We maintain an audit log for role assignment events; sample event IDs are included in the PDF.

If you'd like, we can also provide a short recorded demo (10–12 minutes) showing SCIM provisioning -> role evaluation -> token issuance. Would that be useful for your team?

Regards,
Laura
Senior Security PM
Redwood Inference

(attachment: rbac_scope_matrix.pdf)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jennifer Peters <jennifer.peters@acme.com>, security@acme.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — SCIM & RBAC evidence needed

Jennifer/Tom —

Thanks for the patience. Per your ask we've attached three artifacts:
1) scim_attribute_mapping.csv — minimal required attributes plus notes on optional attributes we preserve.
2) token-lifecycle-diagram.png — shows short-lived tokens for service identities and rotation cadence.
3) rbac_scope_matrix.pdf — maps groups->role templates and highlights manual approval gates for admin elevation.

Short summary for your SIG worksheet:
- SSO/SAML: We support SAML2.0 IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows. MFA enforcement is configurable at the IdP; Redwood enforces second-factor requirements for interactive sessions via the session policy hooks.
- SCIM: Supports SCIM 2.0 with attribute-level mapping. SCIM operations create users and group membership only; they do not directly grant admin roles.
- RBAC & least-privilege: Role templates apply least-privilege by default. Admin-level templates require explicit manual approval (ticket) before assignment; these approval events are logged and retained per our retention policy.
- MFA for machine identities: interactive MFA is not applicable; instead we provide short-lived credentials, rotation requirements, and recommended PKI/JWT signing for integrations.

Next steps: if you'd like the demo recording, we can schedule a 15-minute window this week. Also happy to export a sanitized audit log for the provisioning events if your auditors need it.

—Marcus
Director, Customer Security Programs
Redwood Inference

(attachments: scim_attribute_mapping.csv, rbac_scope_matrix.pdf, token-lifecycle-diagram.png)
